items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Johnny Mitchel, Burns, Joe Hayman, Ted Fields and myself were the most regular customer, of Berry's cafe

ctx.x: Monsieur Berry looked as though he was Hitler's twin brother. The same little moustache and he combed his hair in the same style as Hitler. He was a very nice person and really enjoyed our company.

Johnny Mitchel, Burns, Joe Hayman, Ted Fields and myself were the most regular customer, of Berry's cafe and we must have drank at least a gallon and a half of Dortmund between us every night. I was actually getting a kick out of beer for the first time in my drinking life.

Louis Vola had played bass with Willie in "Chez Florence" but Willie engaged a Cuban bass player named Jose Riestra for the Knocke engagement and I forgot to mention that Bobby Martin had left when I joined Willie. I could understand a little French by now, but Riestra didn't speak English and his French had a Cuban accent which was very hard for me to dig. He was a fine solid bass player and a wonderful person.
